messages.text: How do changes in radar technology affect the measurement capability required from Vector Network Analyzer?

| Area | Supported answer |
|---|---|
| VNA frequency range | The R&S ZNB3020 base range is 9 kHz to 20 GHz, and a frequency-upgrade option extends it to 26.5 GHz [6]. |
| Higher-frequency implication | The R&S ZNB3032 accuracy data covers bands up to >40 GHz to 43.5 GHz measured, so higher-frequency work requires a VNA class with verified accuracy in those upper bands [22]. |
| Dynamic range / low-level transmission | ZNB3020 transmission uncertainty is specified with enhanced dynamic range mode on, including low transmission levels from –50 dB to –60 dB in selected bands [1]. |
| Multiport / S-parameter coverage | The ZNB3020 is available as a 2-port or 4-port vector network analyzer [10]. |
| Calibration discipline | ZNB3020 accuracy validity requires +18 °C to +28 °C, post-calibration temperature change not exceeding 1 °C, identical measurement and calibration frequency points, bandwidth and sweep time, and no interpolation [1]. |
| Higher-frequency calibration discipline | ZNB3032 accuracy validity has the same requirements for temperature range, post-calibration temperature change, identical frequency points, bandwidth and sweep time, and no interpolation [22]. |
| Pulsed measurements | The raw evidence lists pulsed phase-noise measurements, pulse measurement application, and pulse stability measurements [25]. |
| Antenna / radiated measurements | EN 303 981 testing is described as radiated antenna characterization and includes antenna beam pointing, off/on-axis spurious radiation, and receive antenna off-axis gain pattern [7]. |
| Phase stability / phase accuracy | ZNB3020 transmission phase uncertainty is specified, for example, as 0.3° to 1.0° depending on frequency range and transmission level [1]. |
| Higher-frequency phase accuracy | ZNB3032 transmission phase uncertainty is specified up to 1.0° in the >40 GHz to 43.5 GHz measured band [22]. |
【推論】If radar technology moves to higher carrier frequencies, the VNA requirement shifts toward wider verified frequency coverage, because the evidence shows a 20 GHz / 26.5 GHz ZNB3020 class and a ZNB3032 accuracy table extending to 43.5 GHz measured [6][22].
【推論】If radar measurements involve weaker paths, leakage, or isolation-like low transmission levels, the VNA requirement shifts toward enhanced dynamic range and verified low-level uncertainty, because ZNB3020 specifies uncertainty with enhanced dynamic range mode on down to –50 dB to –60 dB transmission levels [1].
【推論】If radar architectures become more antenna-array or beam-oriented, a 2-port or 4-port VNA may need to be complemented by radiated antenna-characterization capability, because the VNA evidence only confirms 2-port/4-port configurations while the antenna evidence covers radiated beam pointing and off-axis measurements [10][7].
